title: Leaked-password protection disabled (Supabase advisor)
description: The Supabase security advisor reports auth_leaked_password_protection disabled, so passwords are not checked against the HaveIBeenPwned breach corpus. This is an Auth dashboard setting not present in source.
claimed_root_cause: HaveIBeenPwned password checking is turned off in Auth settings.

trace.description: Users authenticate with passwords; weak/breached passwords are accepted.

evidence.description: Advisor finding recorded in the manual review write-up.

blockers: Leaked-password protection is a Supabase Auth dashboard setting not represented in the repository.

validation_plan.deployment: In the Supabase dashboard, enable Authentication -> Policies -> 'Leaked password protection' and set a minimum password strength.

title: Self-registration may be enabled at the Auth layer (no in-app signup UI)
description: The app exposes only a login screen (no signup), implying external self-registration should be off. If Supabase Auth 'allow new users to sign up' is enabled, anyone could self-register, obtain the authenticated role, and read all user profiles plus the global catalog tables. Whether signup is enabled is an Auth dashboard setting not present in source.
claimed_root_cause: Auth signup setting may permit self-registration while the product model assumes admin-only account creation (uc-admin-ops).

trace.scope: login-only UI; account creation is admin-only via uc-admin-ops
trace.description: No signup path in the client implies signups should be disabled server-side.
The intended account-creation path is admin-gated; open signup would bypass it.

evidence.description: Only a login card is rendered; there is no self-registration form.

blockers: The Supabase Auth 'allow new users to sign up' setting is a dashboard configuration not represented in the repository.

validation_plan.deployment: In the Supabase dashboard, check Authentication -> Sign In / Providers: confirm 'Allow new users to sign up' is OFF. If it must stay on, restrict allowed email domains and confirm new users receive no implicit project access.

title: Anonymous access to 334 SECURITY DEFINER functions via default PUBLIC EXECUTE
description: Default PostgreSQL PUBLIC EXECUTE plus Supabase's anon role exposed 334 SECURITY DEFINER functions (and 86 trigger functions) to unauthenticated callers over PostgREST /rpc/. Remediated by migration 001: PUBLIC/anon revoked, re-granted to authenticated+service_role, anon limited to token-gated public endpoints and policy helpers (anon-reachable 334 -> 95); trigger functions revoked from all roles.
root_cause: Functions inherited the default PUBLIC EXECUTE grant, which the anon role inherits.
intended_behavior: Unauthenticated callers should reach only the explicit public token endpoints.

trace.description: anon could call internal RPCs before this revoke.
anon re-granted only the intended public endpoints.

evidence.description: Describes the 334 anon-reachable SECURITY DEFINER functions and the lockdown.

instructions: Call internal RPC endpoints with the public anon key.
execution.observed_result: Pre-fix: 334 SECURITY DEFINER functions anon-reachable (most still enforced internal authz). Post-fix: 95 (token endpoints + RLS predicates only); advisor-flagged trigger exposure and mutable search_path both cleared.

remediation.strategy: Revoke PUBLIC/anon, re-grant authenticated+service_role, grant anon only the mapped token endpoints and policy-referenced helpers; revoke trigger functions from all roles; pin search_path. Applied in migration 001.

likelihood.reason: Reachable by anyone with the public anon key (shipped in the client).

impact.reason: Most functions enforce internal authz, so direct data impact was limited; the exposure itself is the defect and attack surface.

confidence.reason: Confirmed via pg_proc privilege queries and Supabase security advisor before/after.

title: Disabled user could self-reactivate by updating their own account_status
description: The profiles self-update policy (USING auth.uid() = id) combined with a guard trigger that froze only is_admin let a disabled/blocked user with a still-valid JWT set their own account_status back to active (and change user_type) via a direct PostgREST UPDATE. Remediated by extending the guard trigger to also freeze account_status, status_reason and user_type for non-admins.
root_cause: The BEFORE UPDATE guard froze only is_admin, not the other admin-controlled profile fields.
intended_behavior: Only an admin may change a user's account_status, status_reason, user_type or is_admin.

trace.description: Disabled accounts are only signed out in the client; a valid JWT can still call the API directly.

conditions.description: A disabled/blocked user whose JWT has not yet expired.
account_status is enforced client-side; self-reactivation defeats that lockout.

execution.attacker_perspective: A user whose account was just disabled/blocked by an admin.
instructions: With the still-valid JWT, PATCH own profiles row setting account_status=active.
execution.observed_result: Pre-fix: the update persisted. Post-fix: the guard trigger reverts account_status/status_reason/user_type for non-admins.

remediation.strategy: Extend prevent_self_admin_escalation to freeze all admin-controlled fields for non-admin callers. Applied in migration 001.

code_changes.fixed_code: -- Step 4: freeze is_admin, account_status, status_reason, user_type for non-admins.

likelihood.reason: Narrow window (valid JWT after disable) and requires direct API use.

impact.reason: Defeats the client-side account lockout; bounded because account_status is not a server-side RLS gate for tenant data.

confidence.reason: Policy + trigger behavior confirmed by source and trigger-binding inspection.

title: Cross-project read leak (IDOR): ~70 tables had SELECT USING (true)
description: Across the execution, finance, material and reporting modules ~70 tables exposed SELECT to every authenticated user regardless of project membership, while writes were correctly project-scoped. Any signed-in user could read other organizations' budgets, cashflow plans, material requisitions, NCRs, statements and daily reports via PostgREST. Remediated by migration 002 and verified with role impersonation (isolated user 206 -> 0 reports; admin unchanged).
root_cause: Read policies were written as USING (true) instead of a project-membership predicate.
intended_behavior: A user may read a project's rows only if they are an admin or a member of that project.

trace.scope: authenticated PostgREST reads of ex_* tables
trace.description: Any authenticated client can select from the exposed tables.
Policies granted unconditional read; now rewritten to ex_can_view()/rasta_user_can_access_master_project().

evidence.description: Enumerates the ~70 affected tables and their corrected per-project read predicates.

conditions.description: Any authenticated user (lowest app role); no project membership required pre-fix.

execution.attacker_perspective: A signed-in user of any one project/organization.
instructions: Sign in as a user who belongs to no project (or a different project).
Query the affected tables through PostgREST.
execution.observed_result: Pre-fix: an unaffiliated user saw all 206 ex_reports (and all budgets/requisitions/statements). Post-fix (migration 002): the same user sees 0; a member sees only their projects; an admin sees all.

remediation.strategy: Rewrite each open SELECT policy to the module's project-view predicate (ex_can_view(project_id) for execution; is_admin_user() OR rasta_user_can_access_master_project(master_project_id) for finance/material/reporting; parent-join for child tables). Applied in migration 002.

code_changes.fixed_code: -- ALTER POLICY <sel> ON <tbl> USING (<project-scoped predicate>); see file for the full per-table map.

likelihood.reason: Trivially reachable by any authenticated user via the public REST API.

impact.reason: Cross-tenant disclosure of commercial/financial data in a multi-organization platform.

confidence.reason: Demonstrated by role impersonation before and after the fix.

title: Known-vulnerable xlsx@0.18.5 reachable via schedule-import parser (prototype pollution, CVE-2023-30533)
description: The scheduling module parses a user-supplied .xlsx file in the browser with SheetJS xlsx@0.18.5. That version is vulnerable to prototype pollution (CVE-2023-30533, fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS (CVE-2024-22363, fixed 0.20.2). A crafted workbook imported by a user can pollute Object.prototype in that user's browser session.
root_cause: A dependency with a published prototype-pollution CVE is used to parse untrusted spreadsheet input, and the npm distribution of xlsx is unmaintained (SheetJS ships current builds only via its own CDN).
intended_behavior: Importing a schedule workbook should parse tabular data only and never let file content mutate the JavaScript runtime (Object.prototype).

trace.description: User selects a schedule file to import.
The untrusted workbook bytes are parsed by xlsx@0.18.5.

evidence.description: Dependency pinned at "xlsx": "^0.18.5" (resolves to 0.18.5, below the 0.19.3 fix).
XLSX.read on user-supplied ArrayBuffer — the reachable parse path.

conditions.description: A signed-in user must import a maliciously crafted .xlsx file (e.g. one sent by a contractor).
Impact depends on xlsx@0.18.5's prototype-pollution behavior; confirmed by the public CVE, not reproduced here.

execution.attacker_perspective: An attacker who can get a target user to import a schedule workbook they supplied.
payloads: A .xlsx crafted per CVE-2023-30533 to set a key on Object.prototype during parse.
instructions: Deliver the crafted .xlsx to a user with schedule-import access.
User opens Scheduling -> Import and selects the file.
On XLSX.read, Object.prototype is polluted in the user's browser session.
execution.observed_result: Not reproduced in-audit (no payload developed, per audit safety rules). The parse path is confirmed reachable and the dependency version is confirmed vulnerable by published CVE.

remediation.strategy: Upgrade off the vulnerable npm build: move to the current SheetJS release (its maintained CDN tarball) or replace the import parser with the already-present exceljs for reading. Keep export usage as-is. Optionally guard parsing by freezing Object.prototype or validating parsed keys.

code_changes.fixed_code: // replace "xlsx": "^0.18.5" with the current SheetJS build, e.g. install from https://cdn.sheetjs.com/ (npm xlsx is stale), or read with the existing exceljs dependency instead.

likelihood.reason: Requires social-engineering a user into importing a crafted workbook; not an unauthenticated or automatic path.

impact.reason: Prototype pollution in the victim's own browser session can corrupt app logic and, with a gadget, escalate to client-side script execution; confined to that one user's session.

confidence.reason: Reachable parse path and vulnerable version are both confirmed in source; only the browser-exploitable end effect is not reproduced.
